mn33:9.2: Orally-recited knowledge, not written books at this time, as emphasized by the word ‘*bahussutā*—learned much’=(lit, ‘heard much’) | *Mātikā* here refers to the two *Pāṭimokkhas*, the fundamental rules for bhikkhus and for bhikkhunis.
mn33:10.2: Alternative translation by Ven. Ñanamoli: ‘does not find inspiration in the meaning, he does not find inspiration in the dhamma, he does not find gladness in the application of the Dhamma’. See Sutta 7, Notes on para. 10, 12, 14, 16.
mn33:13.2: para. 13. abhihatthuṃ pavārenti—invite … to take as much as he likes. P.T.S. Dict. takes ābhīhatthuṃ as a gerund, and Comy. says abhīharitvā pavārenti; but the word’s form is infinitive, and the meaning seems, from the context, to be that they invite (pavārenti) him, with requisites (parikkhārehi) to take (what he likes) (abhihatthuṃ): one who knows the (right) amount leaves some, but one who does not, takes it all. The phrase occurs in the Vinaya (Nissaggiya Pācittiya no. 7).
